title: Keep in-flight VCF Automation requests off a revoked bearer token during a credential rotation
prompt:
Implement `credrotate/client.go` as a standard-library-only Go 1.22+ client for one VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 VCF Automation workflow: rotate the credential a vSphere cloud account authenticates with, and do it without stranding any request that was already in flight on the old API session token.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json`, `docs/official_sources.json` and `credrotate/types.go` before writing anything. VCF Automation, the successor to vRealize and Aria Automation, ships no OpenAPI document in VMware's `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, so this focused contract was transcribed by hand from the rendered xAPIs reference pages at developer.broadcom.com that `docs/official_sources.json` records with a URL, the operation each page documents and the date it was fetched. The contract says so plainly in `x-official-source`: its source is reference documentation, not a published specification. The four `operationId` values are slugs local to that contract, derived from the reference page titles, because VMware publishes none.

Two different secrets are in play and confusing them will cost you the task. The cloud account's own credential — `privateKeyId` and `privateKey` — is the payload being rotated. Your caller's API session credential is the bearer token from `retrieveAuthToken`, and VCF Automation can revoke it at any instant, including in the middle of the rotation you are performing.

The contract names exactly four operations and the loopback mock in `internal/contractmock` serves nothing else; anything off the allow-list answers 404.

- `retrieveAuthToken` — `POST /iaas/api/login`. Unauthenticated: it must not carry an `Authorization` header. The body is a `CspLoginSpecification` and must contain nothing but `refreshToken`. A 200 returns `AuthResponse` with `tokenType` and `token`.
- `updateCloudAccountAsync` — `PATCH /iaas/api/cloud-accounts/{id}`, body `UpdateCloudAccountSpecification`, answering 202 with a `RequestTracker`.
- `getRequestTracker` — `GET /iaas/api/request-tracker/{id}`, answering 200 with a `RequestTracker` whose `status` is `INPROGRESS`, `FINISHED` or `FAILED`.
- `getCloudAccount` — `GET /iaas/api/cloud-accounts/{id}`, answering 200 with a `CloudAccount`.

Every request carries `Accept: application/json` and exactly one query parameter, `apiVersion`, set to `Config.APIVersion`. The contract also declares an optional `$select` on `getCloudAccount`; do not send it. A request with a body carries `Content-Type: application/json` and an exact `Content-Length`, never chunked; a GET carries no body at all. The three authenticated operations carry `Authorization: Bearer {token}`.

`UpdateCloudAccountInput` in `credrotate/types.go` deliberately has no JSON struct tags: the contract, not Go field naming, decides the wire. `Name`, `CloudAccountProperties` and `Regions` are required by `UpdateCloudAccountSpecification` and are always present. Every other member is a pointer and follows one rule — a nil pointer contributes no key whatsoever to the serialized object, while a non-nil pointer contributes its value even when that value is `""`, `false`, `{}` or `[]`. Sending `"description": ""` for an unset `Description`, or `"tags": null`, or `"createDefaultZones": false` for a nil `CreateDefaultZones`, is wrong. The rule recurses: a `Tag` serializes `key` and `value` always and `id` only when `Tag.ID` is non-nil. A `Region` serializes `name` and `externalRegionId`. `CertificateInfo` serializes `certificate`. The verifier compares bodies as a canonical member set with canonical values, so member order and whitespace are yours to choose; membership and values are not.

`RotateCredentials(ctx, cloudAccountID, input)` validates before it opens a connection and issues no HTTP request at all when validation fails, returning an error wrapping `ErrInvalidInput`. Reject an empty `cloudAccountID`, an empty `Name`, a nil `CloudAccountProperties`, an empty `Regions`, any region missing `Name` or `ExternalRegionID`, and any tag missing `Key`. Otherwise it submits the mutation, takes the request id from the accepted `RequestTracker`, polls `getRequestTracker` at `Config.PollInterval` (default one second) for at most `Config.MaxPollAttempts` polls (default 60), and on `FINISHED` reads the account back with `getCloudAccount` and returns it in `RotationResult`. A tracker that reaches `FAILED` yields a `*TrackerError` carrying the request id, the status and the service's message, and no read-back is attempted. A tracker still `INPROGRESS` when the poll budget runs out yields a `*TrackerError` reporting that last observed status.

The rotation and the reads must survive the session credential being revoked underneath them. A 401 on any authenticated operation means the service refused the request before applying anything, so the correct response is to obtain a fresh bearer token and replay that same request once — not to fail the caller, and not to re-submit a mutation the service already accepted. `Client` is used concurrently, so the token and its replacement must be shared safely: `go test -race` is the gate. Above all, a fleet of goroutines that all meet the same revocation must produce exactly one `retrieveAuthToken` exchange between them, not one per goroutine. Track which token generation a request was signed with so a caller that meets a 401 can tell "nobody has refreshed yet, so I must" from "someone already refreshed, so I only replay", and serialize the exchange itself. A request must never go out with a missing, empty or half-written `Authorization` value. `RotationResult.Reauthentications` reports how many extra `retrieveAuthToken` exchanges that one rotation triggered in response to a 401, not counting the lazy first acquisition of a token; `NewClient` itself performs no I/O.

Only `credrotate/client.go` may change. `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...` from the repository root is the acceptance gate and must pass unmodified. Use the standard library only — no third-party modules, no vendoring. The mock binds 127.0.0.1 and the tests read only local files; nothing in this task contacts a live VMware endpoint.

source_basis.note: VCF Automation has no specification in the Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository. docs/contract.json was derived by hand from the Broadcom xAPIs reference pages enumerated in docs/official_sources.json, each recorded with its URL, the operation it documents and the date fetched. The contract states in x-official-source that its source is reference documentation rather than a published specification, and that its operationId values are slugs local to the contract.
source_basis.reference_title: VMware Aria Automation Assembler IaaS API

scenario: A vSphere cloud account's stored privateKeyId and privateKey are rotated through an asynchronous PATCH while the operator's own bearer token is revoked mid-flight; every in-flight request must complete on the reissued token instead of failing on the old secret, and the accepted mutation must not be duplicated by the replay.
environment_note: The contract mock first binds 127.0.0.1:0. If AF_INET is denied by the selected sandbox, its loopback-addressed client dispatches to the identical protected handler in process; neither path can reach a live endpoint.
constraint: The contract-derived loopback allow-list contains only retrieveAuthToken, updateCloudAccountAsync, getRequestTracker and getCloudAccount, and its request log proves the exact wire shape, the omission of unset optional members, the preservation of explicit zero values, single-flight re-authentication under concurrency, and that a 401 replay leaves exactly one accepted mutation.
